sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Detailed study guide and resources for Tughlaq Dynasty: Mohd. Bin Tughlaq are currently being prepared. Check back soon for comprehensive explanations, summary diagrams, and expert preparation recommendations.

Key Dimensions of Study:

  • Definition, scope, and foundational theories.
  • Relevance to General Studies Paper & Contemporary contexts.
  • Core applications and structural framework.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the original personal name of Muhammad bin Tughlaq before ascending the throne?
practiceQuestions.sol: Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the eldest son of Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq and was originally known as Ulugh Khan or Jauna Khan before he assumed power in 1325 AD. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which famous Moroccan traveler visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and was appointed as the Qazi of Delhi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Ibn Battuta, the famous traveler and scholar from Morocco, arrived in Delhi during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign around 1333 AD and served the Sultan as the Qazi of Delhi for several years. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: To which city did Muhammad bin Tughlaq transfer his capital from Delhi in 1327?
practiceQuestions.sol: Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to Devagiri, renaming it Daulatabad, to have a central location that could better control the Deccan territories. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary material used for the token currency introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq in 1329-30?
practiceQuestions.sol: Due to a shortage of silver and his ambitious financial plans, Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced bronze/copper-brass token currency with the same value as gold or silver coins. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the name of the agricultural department established by Muhammad bin Tughlaq to improve cultivation and bring wasteland under tillage?
practiceQuestions.sol: Diwan-i-Kohi was a special department of agriculture set up by Muhammad bin Tughlaq to provide direct state aid, seeds, and loans to cultivators in a model farm tract. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: In which region did Muhammad bin Tughlaq experiment with a heavy tax increase that tragically coincided with a severe famine?
practiceQuestions.sol: Muhammad bin Tughlaq increased taxes in the fertile Ganga-Yamuna Doab region by 10 to 20 times, which unfortunately coincided with a severe drought and famine, leading to extreme peasant distress. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following contemporary historians wrote 'Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi', providing detailed critical accounts of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign?
practiceQuestions.sol: Ziya-ud-din Barani was a court chronicler and thinker who wrote 'Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi', recording the complex policies and ambitious projects of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the name of the agricultural loan distributed by Muhammad bin Tughlaq to farmers during periods of distress?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sondhar (or Taccavi loans) were agricultural loans advanced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq's administration to help peasants buy seeds, cattle, and implements after the Doab famine. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: At which place did Muhammad bin Tughlaq die in 1351 while campaigning against rebellious elements?
practiceQuestions.sol: Muhammad bin Tughlaq died in 1351 at Thatta in Sindh while leading a military expedition to suppress the rebellion of Taghi, a Turkish slave. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which famous contemporary saint and Sufi mystic did Muhammad bin Tughlaq have a strained relationship with, often refusing to meet him in Delhi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Although Nizamuddin Auliya passed away just before Tughlaq ascended the throne, the tense dynamic between Sufi saints and the state persisted, and Tughlaq famously clashed with other spiritual leaders like Shaikh Nasiruddin Mahmud (Chirag-i Delhi). [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token currency experiment ultimately fail, leading to widespread economic disruption?
opts: The public refused to use copper coins and continued hoarding gold and silver.
Widespread counterfeiting of bronze/copper coins occurred because the state failed to maintain a monopoly on minting.
Foreign merchants refused to accept Indian goods in exchange for token currency.
The Sultan ordered the immediate destruction of all mint houses across the empire.
practiceQuestions.sol: The core failure of the token currency scheme was the inability of the Sultanate to prevent the private minting of bronze coins. Every household virtually became a mint, as the design was simple and unencrypted, flooding the market with fake coins and depreciating their value. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the underlying strategic and administrative rationale behind Muhammad bin Tughlaq's decision to shift his capital to Daulatabad?
opts: To escape the harsh winters of Northern India.
To establish a central administrative hub capable of effectively controlling the expanding southern and central provinces.
To protect Delhi from impending Mongol naval invasions along the western coast.
To hand over Delhi entirely to the Sufi orders and religious scholars.
practiceQuestions.sol: Daulatabad's central geographical position relative to the whole of India made it a strategic choice for the Sultan to administer both Northern and Southern territories directly, though the execution proved disastrous. [PrimaryReference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Muhammad bin Tughlaq's approach towards governance and religious law (Sharia) differ from that of his predecessors like Ala-ud-din Khalji?
opts: He completely abolished Islamic jurisprudence and instituted Mongol legal codes.
He attempted to rationalize laws and rely on secular intellect/royal decrees, while still maintaining formal allegiance to the Caliphate.
He ran a strict theocracy dictated entirely by orthodox Ulemas.
He banned all religious conversions and declared himself the supreme prophet.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike Ala-ud-din who kept religion separate from statecraft ('Kingship knows no kinship'), Muhammad bin Tughlaq sought validation from the Abbasid Caliph while simultaneously using independent reason and secular royal decrees (Zawabit) in governance. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did the taxation experiment in the Doab region fail so disastrously under Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
opts: The local zamindars refused to collect taxes and revolted collectively.
An arbitrary tax enhancement coincided with severe drought and famine, and oppressive tax collection methods aggravated peasant flight.
The Sultan replaced all agrarian land taxes with a flat tax on religious pilgrimages.
The revenue department was entirely staffed by inexperienced foreign merchants.
practiceQuestions.sol: The harsh enhancement of revenue demand in the fertile Doab occurred just when rains failed and crops withered. Instead of granting relief, rigid tax collectors used coercion, prompting peasants to burn crops and flee into forests. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the principal outcome of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's ambitious Khurasan expedition plan?
opts: A resounding military victory that expanded the Delhi Sultanate to Central Asia.
The massive army of over 300,000 soldiers was disbanded after payment of a year's advance salary, draining the royal treasury without any territorial gain.
An alliance with the Mongols that permanently secured the northern borders.
The complete annexation of Persia and Iraq into the Indian tax system.
practiceQuestions.sol: Tughlaq assembled a huge army to conquer Khurasan and Iraq, paying them a full year's salary in advance. However, political conditions in Central Asia changed before the march began, and the army had to be disbanded, wasting immense state resources. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Muhammad bin Tughlaq's religious and social policy differ from orthodox Islamic norms of the era?
opts: He was the first Sultan to actively participate in Hindu festivals like Holi and ban animal slaughter on certain days.
He strictly banned Sufi orders from operating within Delhi city limits.
He instituted forced conversions of all high-caste Hindu nobles.
He forced all Muslim Ulema to wear saffron robes.
practiceQuestions.sol: Muhammad bin Tughlaq was known for his liberal outlook, participating in Hindu festivals (such as Holi) and being the first Delhi Sultan to visit the temple of Ajmer. He also prohibited certain social practices like sati (with conditional permission) and interacted freely with non-Muslim scholars like Jains and Yogis. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What does Barani's and Ibn Battuta's descriptions of Muhammad bin Tughlaq as a 'mixture of opposites' signify?
opts: He suffered from a dual personality disorder that rendered him medically unfit to rule.
His character combined immense intellect, piety, and generosity with extreme cruelty, impatience, and erratic decision-making.
He switched his religious faith between Sunni Islam and Shia Islam every alternate year.
He was an absolute pacifist in foreign policy while being a ruthless dictator at home.
practiceQuestions.sol: Contemporary writers noted that Tughlaq was exceptionally learned, well-read in philosophy, mathematics, and medicine, yet his erratic policies, severe punishments, and inability to tolerate dissent earned him the reputation of being a 'mixture of opposites'. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Muhammad bin Tughlaq's Qarachil expedition (against the Kumaon-Garhwal region) end in disaster?
opts: The imperial forces were completely annihilated by heavy mountain snows and guerrilla warfare after initial success.
The hill chieftains surrendered unconditionally, causing severe financial losses due to unpaid war booty.
The expeditionary force mutinied and joined hands with the Mongol invaders.
The commanders refused to cross the foothills of the Himalayas.
practiceQuestions.sol: Launched to bring the Kumaon-Garhwal hill tribes under control, the expedition achieved early success but was decimated by the harsh Himalayan winter, lack of provisions, and fierce mountain warfare, with very few soldiers surviving to return. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the provincial revolts during the later years of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign reshape the political map of India?
opts: They resulted in the immediate unification of the entire Indian subcontinent under the Delhi Sultanate.
They led to the breakaway of key provinces, giving birth to independent regional kingdoms like the Bahmani Kingdom and the Vijayanagara Empire.
They forced the Sultan to abdicate in favor of a Mongol prince.
They led to the complete dissolution of the Turkish nobility and establishment of a republic.
practiceQuestions.sol: Tughlaq's administrative instability and harsh measures caused widespread rebellions. During his lifetime, the Deccan witnessed the foundation of the Vijayanagara Empire (1336) and the Bahmani Kingdom (1347), alongside the independence of Bengal and Madurai. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of Muhammad bin Tughlaq receiving a patent of investiture from the Abbasid Caliph in Egypt?
opts: It was done to legitimize his rule in the eyes of orthodox Muslims and religious scholars who questioned his authority.
It was a demand made by the Caliph to collect annual tribute from India.
It allowed him to legally dissolve the Islamic legal system and declare himself Caliph.
It was a commercial treaty allowing free trade between Delhi and Cairo.
practiceQuestions.sol: Although the Abbasid Caliphate in Baghdad had collapsed earlier, a branch existed in Cairo. Tughlaq sought and received formal investiture from the Cairo Caliph to strengthen his political legitimacy against domestic rebellions and orthodox critics. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Muhammad bin Tughlaq's administrative experiments:
1. He introduced token currency made of bronze and copper due to a worldwide silver shortage and depletion of the royal treasury.
2. He set up a dedicated agricultural department called Diwan-i-Kohi to provide state support and loans to farmers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token currency was necessitated by silver shortages and heavy expenditures, and Diwan-i-Kohi was indeed established to improve agriculture in a model tract by distributing taccavi loans. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ibn Battuta:
1. He was a traveler from Morocco who visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
2. He recorded his observations and travel experiences in a book titled 'Kitab-i-Rahla'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Ibn Battuta arrived in India in 1333, served as Delhi's Qazi, and his travelogue 'Kitab-i-Rahla' remains a vital primary source for studying Tughlaq administration and society. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the transfer of capital by Muhammad bin Tughlaq:
1. The capital was shifted from Delhi to Devagiri (renamed Daulatabad) to ensure better administrative control over the Deccan.
2. The entire population of Delhi was forcibly ordered to migrate twice—once to Daulatabad and later back to Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate historical accounts according to chronicles like Barani and Ibn Battuta. The forced migration caused immense hardship, and the subsequent reversal added to the misery. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Doab tax hike:
1. The tax enhancement in the Ganga-Yamuna Doab was accompanied by a severe famine caused by failure of monsoons.
2. The Sultan successfully mitigated the crisis by waiving all land revenues and distributing free grain from royal granaries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: taxes were raised in the Doab concurrently with a severe famine. Statement 2 is incorrect because the local officials enforced tax collection rigidly, causing immense distress before the Sultan realized his mistake and provided late relief. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad bin Tughlaq's religious and cultural outlook:
1. He was deeply read in Jainism, philosophy, and logic, and engaged in philosophical discussions with Jain scholars like Jina Prabha Suri.
2. He strictly forbade Hindus from celebrating any public festivals throughout the Sultanate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Tughlaq was very scholarly and patronized Jain scholars. Statement 2 is incorrect because he was remarkably liberal, participating in festivals like Holi, making statement 2 false. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the military expeditions of Muhammad bin Tughlaq:
1. The Khurasan expedition was undertaken with a large standing army to conquer Central Asia, but was eventually abandoned.
2. The Qarachil expedition was launched against the hill tribes of the Himalayas to secure the northern frontier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Both the Khurasan and Qarachil expeditions are notable examples of Tughlaq's grand strategic designs that suffered from heavy logistical failures and drainage of state funds. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements concerning the rebellions during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign:
1. The Deccan witnessed the emergence of the independent Bahmani Kingdom and Vijayanagara Empire during his tenure.
2. The Sultan successfully suppressed all regional revolts and died as the undisputed ruler of an expanded Indian empire.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Vijayanagara (1336) and Bahmani (1347) broke away during his reign. Statement 2 is incorrect because he failed to suppress several major revolts and died while campaigning against a rebel in Sindh. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the character and assessments of Muhammad bin Tughlaq:
1. Contemporary historian Ziya-ud-din Barani portrayed him as a ruler who combined contradictory traits of benevolence, cruelty, wisdom, and folly.
2. Modern historians view him as a visionary ahead of his time whose administrative reforms failed primarily due to poor planning and implementation deficits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Barani captured his erratic duality, while modern historiography recognizes that many of his ideas (like token currency, agricultural loans, and empire centralization) were sound in theory but disastrously executed. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the coinage and economic measures of Muhammad bin Tughlaq:
1. He earned the title 'Prince of Moneyers' from a modern numismatist due to the sheer variety, design, and circulation of coins issued during his reign.
2. His token currency experiment failed because the state established foolproof security marks that prevented any private counterfeiting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Edward Thomas termed him 'Prince of Moneyers' due to remarkable numismatic innovations. Statement 2 is incorrect because the complete lack of security marks and easy replication caused rampant counterfeiting, leading to the experiment's failure. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India / Numismatic Studies]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the death and succession of Muhammad bin Tughlaq:
1. He died in 1351 at Thatta while suppressing a rebellion led by Taghi in Sindh.
2. He was immediately succeeded by his capable cousin Firoz Shah Tughlaq, who was chosen by the nobles and the army.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Tughlaq died in Sindh in 1351, and following a brief succession crisis, Firoz Shah Tughlaq was chosen as Sultan by the army and nobles to restore stability. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/11 Medieval India]
